Title: DIY Repair of a Broken Smartphone Screen

A nifty online tool helps you with repairing your Smartphone on your own.
You start by entering the model and what is broken.
The tool gives you the list of materials, the list of tools, and (for each part) several ordering choices.
Some stuff you already have (e.g. some tools, screws).
The tool also lets you contact friends if you can borrow / buy something for cheap from them.
The rest you buy.
Afterwards you receive instructions how to fix your phone.
If it worked, send a review and/or video of you fixing it.
If it hasn't worked out, you can send it to an expert.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Compare the model with the description; remove unsupported elements and retain every explicitly stated alternative, outcome and collaboration.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes activities or outcomes by their action, object, recipient, or stage: Use BPMN labels that preserve those stated distinctions rather than substituting a different action or outcome.

When the description states an activity or outcome whose surrounding context is already clear from the process flow: Use a concise BPMN label that preserves the activity or outcome, without adding explanatory context that does not distinguish it from other elements.

When the description explicitly states an activity’s action, object, recipient, or multiple coordinated actions: Preserve those stated details in the BPMN task label rather than omitting or substituting them.

When the description explicitly states an action performed by a participant, and a related receipt or outcome could be mistaken for that action: Label the BPMN activity with the stated action and preserve its direction; do not replace it with the corresponding action from another participant’s perspective.
